chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhariyy from Salamah ibn Hayyan from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is the night of Friday, recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in the Maghrib prayer. And when it is in the last (Isha) prayer, recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and 'Sabbih Isma Rabbika al-A'la'. When it is the dawn prayer on Friday, recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad'. When it is the Friday congregational prayer, recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun. And when it is the afternoon prayer on Friday, recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad'.'
And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id) from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Recite Al-Jumu'ah and 'Sabbih Isma Rabbika al-A'la' on the night of Friday, and in the dawn prayer recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad', and in the Friday congregational prayer recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun.'
And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id) from Safwan from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is there a specific time for recitation in the prayer?' He said: 'No, except in Friday, where Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun are recited in it.'

key_terms.سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى: Sabbih Isma Rabbika al-A'la (Opening of Surah Al-A'la, Chapter 87)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Surah Al-Ikhlas, Chapter 112)
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْجُمُعَةِ: Night of Friday (from Maghrib until dawn)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended Quranic recitations for each prayer on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific *mustahabb* (recommended) Quranic recitations for the five daily prayers on Friday, highlighting a unique emphasis on Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah Al-Munafiqun during the congregational Dhuhr prayer. The repetition of Surah Al-Jumu'ah across multiple prayers underscores its thematic relevance to the day's spiritual significance, while the inclusion of Al-Munafiqun in the main prayer serves as a reminder of hypocrisy, a key theme in Friday sermons. This practice reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing Friday's ritual acts through specific textual recitations that enhance the worshipper's connection to the Imam and the divine attributes associated with the day.
